counterexamples.evidence: Run 1 served text: 'keep the 7-shaped double threat alive by playing the square that matters later in your forced line' wrapped in [zone:future:c2r5]. On the decision board 333222 column 2 is empty (ht row = 0), so a move there lands at c2r1; c2r5 is filled only at ply ~36 of the engine own finalMovestring 33322232332414001244445556666660011, where it is the empty completing cell of the Green row-5 four c2r5/c3r5(X11)/c4r5(X9)/c5r5(X21). The prompt states Better move: column 4 (lands at c4r4) at line 3 and warns at line 78 never to describe a matters-later handle as something happening right now.

Run 3 served text says only 'the better move preserves the later line...' and never names column 4 in prose; the better-col handle was offered on the decision board but not used, so the blunderer is told what was preserved but not which column to play. Same defect drives the run 1 A6 mechanical fail.

Guardrail: 'You gave up a win AND handed the opponent their own; name both lines with their horizons.' Run 1 names neither line explicitly (only 'your winning line is gone') and omits the required you-key-line handle, although the prompt marks it MUST-appear at line 87-88.
